summary: Setup is moderate: registration is self-serve, but any public user can connect only after Google verifies the app when it uses Gmail sensitive or restricted scopes. Restricted scopes add an annual third-party security assessment if data is accessed through a server.
timeToProduction: 1–2 weeks with sensitive scopes only; several weeks or more with restricted scopes.
effort: 2–4 days of work, including the demo video and privacy policy
cost: Free with sensitive scopes only; restricted scopes add a third-party security assessment, with a fee set by the assessor.

gates.title: Any Google account with a Cloud project can register
Testing mode caps you at 100 test users and expires authorizations after 7 days
gates.what: Apps in Testing status only work for listed test users (up to 100), and authorizations expire after 7 days.
gates.where: Google Cloud console, Google Auth Platform, Audience page. The developer adds test users.
gates.todo: Add your own and your testers' Google accounts as test users while developing. Publish and verify the app before opening to real users.

gates.title: Google must verify the app before the public can grant Gmail scopes
gates.what: Sensitive Gmail scopes need OAuth verification (typically 3–5 business days). Restricted scopes need verification that can take several weeks.
gates.where: Google Cloud console, Google Auth Platform: Branding and Verification Center. The developer submits.
gates.todo: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes, declare them on the Data Access page, verify branding, then submit a scope justification and demo video.

gates.title: Workspace admins can block your app until they trust it
gates.what: A Google Workspace admin can block any app. If an app requests a restricted service and the admin hasn't trusted it, users can't add it.
gates.where: Google Admin console, Security, Access and data control, API controls, Manage Third-Party App Access. The customer's organization admin acts here.
gates.todo: Give customers your OAuth client ID so their admin can mark the app Trusted.

gates.title: Gmail API use has no paid tier requirement
Restricted-scope apps must be reassessed every 12 months
gates.what: Restricted-scope apps must be reverified and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months, or lose access to the verified restricted scopes.
gates.where: Google emails the team when recertification is due. The developer acts.
gates.todo: Keep the project's contact emails current so the notice is not missed.

requirements.text: A Google account and a Google Cloud project to hold the OAuth consent screen and client.
A domain you own, verified in Google Search Console, for the app's authorized domains.
A publicly accessible home page and a privacy policy on the same domain.
A demo video uploaded to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.text: Sign in to the Google Cloud console and create or select a project for the app.
steps.why: Separate projects for testing and production let you submit the production project for verification cleanly.
steps.detail: Use an account that will remain Owner or Editor of the project.

steps.text: Choose the audience: External for users outside your organization, or Internal for your Workspace organization only.
steps.why: External is available to any Google Account. Internal limits authorization to organization members; others get an org_internal error. An app for outside users needs External.

steps.text: Fill in the Branding fields: app name, logo, support email, developer contact, home page and privacy policy links.
steps.why: These appear on the consent screen.
steps.detail: Make the home page public and host the privacy policy on the same domain.

steps.text: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes for your features and declare them on the Data Access page.
steps.why: Scope class sets the verification burden: non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted.
steps.detail: Use gmail.send rather than gmail.modify if you only send mail.

steps.text: Create an OAuth client ID (Web application) on the Clients page with your redirect URIs.
Add your test accounts as test users and connect your own account.
steps.why: In Testing status only listed test users can authorize.
steps.detail: Authorizations expire after 7 days in Testing, so reconnect weekly.

steps.text: Verify your domain in Search Console, then click Verify Branding and then Publish branding.
steps.why: Brand verification shows your app name and logo on the consent screen.
steps.detail: Publish within 7 days of a passing result or rerun the check.

steps.text: Write the scope justification text and the demo video script.
steps.why: Each scope needs a justification and an explanation of why a narrower scope is not sufficient.

steps.text: Record the demo video and upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.
Submit the app for data access verification in the OAuth Verification Center.
steps.detail: Check the developer contact and support emails for Google's questions.
About 3–5 business days for sensitive scopes; restricted scopes can take several weeks.

blockers.problem: Users see an unverified app warning and sign-ups stop at 100.
blockers.fix: Complete verification for all sensitive and restricted scopes you request. The cap is lifetime for the project and cannot be reset.

blockers.problem: A restricted scope triggers a security assessment you did not plan for.
blockers.fix: Check whether a sensitive scope covers your features. If you must use restricted scopes and data passes through a server, plan for the annual third-party assessment.

blockers.problem: Users in Workspace organizations cannot authorize the app.
blockers.fix: Ask their admin to mark your OAuth client ID as Trusted in API controls.

blockers.problem: Testing tokens stop working after a week.
blockers.fix: Reconnect test users, or publish and verify the app.

blockers.problem: Branding check passed but later shows Need to re-verify.
blockers.fix: Click Publish branding within 7 days of a passing result, or rerun the check.

couldNotVerify: Google says billing for exceeding Gmail API quota limits will be announced later in 2026; the pricing is not yet published.

claims.statement: Gmail scopes are classed as non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted, each with a different verification burden.
claims.sourceTitle: Choose Gmail API scopes | Google for Developers
claims.quote: Generally, you should choose the most narrowly focused scope possible and avoid requesting scopes that your app doesn't require.
claims.note: The page's scope tables list the classes.

claims.statement: Sensitive scope verification typically takes 3-5 business days.
claims.sourceTitle: Sensitive scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete.

claims.statement: Restricted scope verification can take several weeks, with an annual third-party security assessment if data is accessed through a server.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: For this reason, the restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete.

claims.statement: Gmail API standard use is at no additional cost.
claims.sourceTitle: Usage limits | Gmail | Google for Developers
claims.quote: All standard use of the Gmail API is available at no additional cost.

claims.statement: External projects are available to any user with a Google Account.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Projects configured with a user type of External are available to any user with a Google Account.
claims.note: No business account, paid plan or approval is mentioned for registering.

claims.statement: Testing status is limited to 100 test users and authorizations expire after seven days.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent.
claims.note: The same page states the 100 test user limit.

claims.statement: Testing is the default publishing status for development and limits the app to listed test users.
claims.sourceTitle: Sensitive scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: This setting means that your app is still in development and is only available to users you add to the list of test users.

claims.statement: Verification needs a demo video uploaded to YouTube as Unlisted.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: If any of your OAuth clients aren't ready for production, we suggest that you delete them from the project that's requesting verification.
claims.note: Same page describes the Unlisted YouTube video requirement and recommends separate test and production projects.

claims.statement: Sensitive scopes need a justification for each scope and why a narrower scope is not sufficient.
claims.sourceTitle: Sensitive scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: Sensitive scopes require review by Google before any Google Account can grant access.
claims.note: The submission steps ask for per-scope justification.

claims.statement: Workspace admins can block any OAuth app.
claims.sourceTitle: OAuth app state overview | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: In essence, Google's verification process is a signal of general policy compliance, but the Google Workspace administrator has the ultimate authority on whether an app can access their organization's data.

claims.statement: If an app requests a restricted service and the admin hasn't trusted it, users can't add it.
claims.sourceTitle: Control which third-party & internal apps access Google Workspace data | Apps & integrations | Google Workspace Help
claims.quote: While users are prompted to consent to apps, if an app requests access to a restricted service and you haven't specifically trusted the app, users can't add it.

claims.statement: No paid plan or tier requirement is mentioned for Gmail API production use.
claims.sourceTitle: Usage limits | Gmail | Google for Developers
claims.note: Page says standard use is free; absence of a required paid tier inferred.

claims.statement: Restricted-scope apps must be reverified and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: As mentioned previously, to keep access to any verified restricted scopes, apps must be reverified for compliance and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months after your assessor's Letter of Assessment (LOA) approval date.

claims.statement: Google emails the team when it is time to recertify.
claims.sourceTitle: Restricted scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: The Google review team emails you when it is time to recertify your app.

claims.statement: Home page must be public and privacy policy hosted on the same domain.
claims.sourceTitle: Sensitive scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your site's logged-in users.
claims.note: Same page requires the privacy policy on the same domain and domain ownership verified in Search Console.

claims.statement: Internal user type limits authorization to organization members; others get org_internal error.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: An org_internal authorization error is displayed when authorization is requested from users outside the Google Cloud project's parent.

claims.statement: OAuth clients are created from the Credentials page via Create credentials, OAuth client ID.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating client IDs | Cloud Endpoints Frameworks for App Engine | Google Cloud Documentation
claims.quote: Select Web application as the application type.
claims.note: Page is for Endpoints Frameworks and older console flow; newer docs use the Clients page.

claims.statement: Passing branding results are valid for 7 days before they must be published or rerun.
claims.sourceTitle: Sensitive scope verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: Click the Publish branding button to make the new branding live.
claims.note: Adjacent note on the page states results are valid for 7 days.

claims.statement: Unverified apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes have a lifetime cap of 100 new users that cannot be reset.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: The user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed.
